clue.text: Explorer held by tribal boatmen

indicators.note: held by says the answer is kept within the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of tribal into the start of boatmen

explanation.surface: A traveller in unknown lands is carried along by native rowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Vasco Núñez de Balboa was the Spanish explorer who reached the Pacific overland in 1513.
explanation.definitionFit: Balboa was a conquistador, the first European known to sight the Pacific from the Americas, so he is an example of an explorer.

clue.text: A legal procedure cut short in courts

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a legal procedure in court

explanation.surface: A court case is curtailed while proceedings take place in courtrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' looks like law courts after 'legal procedure', but here it means open courtyards in a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court or hall in a building, so the plural form means courtyards.

clue.text: Like most MPs, needing support with seat

parts.note: to back is to support
a bench is a long seat

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament mostly need backing and somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: Backbench MPs are those without a ministerial or shadow post, who sit on the rear benches of the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Most British Members of Parliament hold no government office and are described with this adjective after where they sit.

clue.text: Albatross initially going by railway, in large birdcage

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its first letter
via means going by way of

explanation.surface: A seabird travels by train and ends up in a large cage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a big enclosure in which birds are kept, a walk-in version of a cage.

clue.text: Lateral pass at football for colleague

parts.note: lateral means at the side
a kick is how the ball is passed in football

explanation.surface: A sideways pass in a football match goes to a team-mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, the partner one works alongside.

clue.text: Weekly publication shaping up as lengthy read

indicators.note: shaping means the following letters are being formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Sunday newspaper is building up into a long read.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter names the very paper the puzzle appeared in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday Telegraph is a British newspaper that comes out once every seven days.

clue.text: Challenge about European rule in Eastern state

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the others

parts.note: a dare is a challenge
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A dispute over European regulation in a state in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a small US state on the Atlantic coast, in the eastern part of the country.

clue.text: Opener bagging runs repeatedly for county

indicators.note: bagging means the first word holds the letters inside it

parts.note: a key opens a lock
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
repeatedly means the runs letter appears a second time

explanation.surface: A cricket opening batsman piles up runs for his county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a cricket batsman, but it is something that opens a lock. Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerry is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Kind of ladder on board for mate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., or companionway, is a ship's staircase between decks
second meaning: a friend or partner

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means aboard a ship, and 'mate' also suggests a ship's officer, which helps the nautical misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who keeps you company and the stairway linking decks on a vessel.

clue.text: Like stories about king, producing resistance to movement

indicators.note: about means the first word wraps around the letter

parts.note: fictional describes made-up stories
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Tales about a monarch meet some opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is the force that resists one surface sliding over another, and the adjective describes what causes it.

clue.text: A swindle, i.e. something not on the level

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in British slang a ... is a racket or swindle
second meaning: a sloping surface joining two levels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' reads as dishonest, which echoes the swindle, but in the second sense it means literally sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an inclined surface between heights and, in British slang, a fraudulent scheme.

clue.text: Has potential to emerge as right artist for capital

parts.note: can means to be able to
to be is to turn out as
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone shows promise of becoming the right painter for the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the seat of the Australian government, the country's chief city by status.

clue.text: With style, arrange buttonhole

parts.note: a way is a manner or style
to lay is to arrange, as in laying a table

explanation.surface: A flower for the lapel is arranged with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttonhole' suggests a flower worn on a jacket, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to stop and detain them in conversation, just as to waylay is to intercept them.

clue.text: Part of play heard, or otherwise perceived

indicators.note: heard means the word must be said aloud, giving one spelt differently

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: Part of a play is listened to, or else watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' contrasts with 'heard': the answer means perceived by the eye rather than the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen is the past participle of see, so it means noticed by sight, a way of perceiving other than hearing.

clue.text: Article I tailored in special way

indicators.note: in special way means the letters of the fodder are arranged differently

explanation.surface: An item of clothing altered to a custom fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' and 'tailored' together suggest a garment, but the article is in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is a newspaper's leading article giving the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Reptile quietly moving into stretch of land

indicators.note: moving into means the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of land
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A reptile creeps silently into a tract of country.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, so it is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: 100 in calculation that's difficult to eliminate

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: something that is difficult to eliminate

indicators.note: in means the number goes inside the sum

parts.note: addition is a kind of calculation
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A sum with a hundred in it proves hard to get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a dependency or habit that a person finds very hard to give up.

clue.text: Judge Tory party right

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
a side is a party in a dispute

explanation.surface: A judge rules that the Conservative party is in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a noun at the head of the sentence, but the definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to weigh it up and form an opinion, which is what judging means here.

clue.text: Is one wise to avoid early retirement?

definitions.text: Is one wise to avoid early retirement?

parts.words: Is one wise to avoid early retirement?
parts.note: owls are proverbially wise, and early retirement means going to bed early, which this person avoids

explanation.walkthrough: 'Early retirement' suggests leaving work young, but it means turning in for the night; the wise one is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who habitually stays up late rather than going to bed early.

clue.text: Refuse to admit study leads to faulty conclusion

parts.note: a den is a private room for study

indicators.note: conclusion means only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone won't concede that their research produced a flawed result.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to reject it or decline to accept that it is true.

clue.text: Rod on bottom, intended to sting

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits above the second in this down answer

parts.note: a bar is a rod of metal
a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

explanation.surface: A fishing rod rests on the riverbed, ready to hook something.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed remark is a pointed one meant to wound or hurt the person it is aimed at.

clue.text: Some who use stages in theatres

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some performers use the stages in theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is the auditorium of a theatre or its audience, as in a full house.

clue.text: Some unceremonious language

indicators.note: Some signals that only part of the following letters is taken, a run hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of unceremonious into the start of language

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both hides the answer and describes it: slang is informal, casual speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal vocabulary, the opposite of formal or polite speech.

clue.text: Part of vehicle in which to carry clothes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the casing that encloses a vehicle's gears
second meaning: read playfully, a case for gear, which is informal for clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, a suitcase for one's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the metal housing protecting a gearbox, and jokingly a bag for kit and clothing.

clue.text: Extended accounts unchanged when set up

parts.note: long narratives, and the word reads the same backwards

explanation.surface: Long stories stay the same however they are presented.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse tale of heroes and families.

clue.text: Card is ace, put on five

indicators.note: put on means the following letters are attached after the first in this across answer

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A player lays an ace on top of a five in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' suggests a playing card after 'ace' and 'five', but the answer is a credit card brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Visa is a well-known brand of credit or debit card.

clue.text: Select card-game — one's raised to shut opponents out

definitions.text: one's raised to shut opponents out

parts.note: to draw is to select, as in drawing lots
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Choose a card game in which one player lifts their cards to keep rivals out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a card player's tactic but describes a castle's lifting bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is hinged and hauled up to stop attackers crossing a moat into a castle.

clue.text: Powerful man in love with awfully rich gal

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: awfully means the following letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mighty man is besotted with a dreadfully wealthy girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of a small ruling group, a wealthy and influential person.

clue.text: European language — found around part of UK

indicators.note: found around means the first piece is discovered wrapped about the second

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is itself a dash
NI is Northern Ireland, a part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A continental tongue is discovered being spoken in a corner of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash looks like mere punctuation between definition and wordplay, but the setter makes the symbol itself the outer piece; Northern Ireland is the part of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish is the Scandinavian tongue spoken in Denmark, so it is an example of a language of Europe.
